   207	  printf '%s' "${PROJECT_ROOT}/.run/.dec-write-${h}.lock"

   209	acquire_lock(){ # target
   210	  local lp; lp="$(lock_path "$1")"
   211	  mkdir -p "${PROJECT_ROOT}/.run"
   212	  if command -v flock >/dev/null 2>&1 && [[ "${LOA_DEC_NO_FLOCK:-0}" != "1" ]]; then
   213	    exec 9>"$lp"
   214	    flock -w "$LOCK_WAIT" 9 || die "lock busy: another writer holds ${lp} (waited ${LOCK_WAIT}s); retry"
   215	    return 0
   216	  fi
   217	  local d="${lp}.d" tries=$(( LOCK_WAIT * 10 )) pid
   218	  while ! mkdir "$d" 2>/dev/null; do
   219	    pid="$(cat "$d/pid" 2>/dev/null || true)"
   220	    # Stale: older than 60 s and its owner is gone.
   221	    if [[ -n "$(find "$d" -maxdepth 0 -mmin +1 2>/dev/null)" ]] && { [[ -z "$pid" ]] || ! kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null; }; then
   222	      rm -f "$d/pid" 2>/dev/null; rmdir "$d" 2>/dev/null || true; continue
   223	    fi
   224	    tries=$(( tries - 1 ))
   225	    (( tries > 0 )) || die "lock busy: another writer holds ${d} (waited ${LOCK_WAIT}s); retry"
   226	    sleep 0.1
   227	  done
   228	  MKLOCK="$d"
   229	  printf '%s\n' "$$" > "$d/pid"
   230	}

   288	# Resolve an artifact path from a flatline:/dissent: ref; prints the absolute path or dies.
   289	artifact_path(){ # voice path

   307	# Sets VOICE, REF, SHA from --as / --answer-ref and the context. $1 = allow_as (1 at creation).

   309	derive_attribution(){
   310	  local allow_as="$1" as ref

   393	verify_and_swap(){
   394	  local old="$1" added="$2" touched="$3" errs
   395	  # Whole-ledger JSON goes through files (--slurpfile): a large ledger overflows one argv string.
   396	  SCRATCH="$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/dec-verify.XXXXXX")"

   399	  errs="$(jq -rn --slurpfile O "${SCRATCH}.old" --slurpfile N "${SCRATCH}.new" --argjson added "$added" --argjson t "$touched" '
   400	    $O[0] as $o | $N[0] as $n

   409	        ($o.decisions[] as $r | select($ts[$r.id] | not) | select($nb[$r.id] != $r) | "row \($r.id) changed outside this operation"),
   410	        ($n.decisions[] | .id as $x | select($os[$x] | not) | select($ts[$x] | not) | "unexpected new row \($x)")

   412	  [[ -z "$errs" ]] || die "ABORT: ${errs//$'\n'/; }; ledger untouched"

   424	# Build a new row JSON. Args: id status voice ref sha supersedes
   425	build_row(){

   428	  summary="$(san1 "$(o summary)")"; phase="$(san1 "$(o phase)")"; category="$(san1 "$(o category)")"; source="$(san1 "$(o source)")"

   448	    {id: $id, created_at: $now, updated_at: $now, phase: $phase, category: $category, summary: $summary,
   449	     decision: ($decision | n), rationale: ($rationale | n),
   450	     alternatives_considered: (if ($alts | length) == 0 then null else $alts end), consequences: $cons,
   451	     proposed_by: $voice, decided_by: null, decided_by_ref: ($ref | n), evidence_sha256: ($sha | n),
   452	     recorded_by: $rb, commit: $commit, source: $source, cycle: ($cycle | n), supersedes: ($sup | n),
   453	     supersede_proposed_by: null, status: $status,

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# tools/check-round-independence.sh: is an interview transcript asked in
     4	# prerequisite-ordered rounds?
     5	#
     6	# In `interview.pacing: rounds` every round of questions ends with one comment
     7	# block (discovering-requirements/resources/REFERENCE.md §Question Pacing):
     8	#
     9	#   <!-- round: 2; questions: [{"id":"Q4","depends_on":[]},{"id":"Q2","depends_on":[],"reasked":true}] -->
    10	#
    11	# This checker reads those blocks from a transcript (markdown or plain text,
    12	# one block per line) and fails when:
    13	#   * a `depends_on` names a question asked in the same round,
    14	#   * a `depends_on` names a question not asked in an earlier round,
    15	#   * a non-reasked id repeats, or a `reasked` id was never asked before,
    16	#   * round numbers do not increase, or a block is malformed,
    17	#   * the rounds average fewer than --min-average new questions (default 2).
    18	# `reasked` entries are skipped for id uniqueness and for the average. The
    19	# final round is exempt from the average when there are two or more rounds.
    20	#
    21	# Usage:
    22	#   tools/check-round-independence.sh <transcript> [--min-average N] [--json]
    23	#
    24	# Exit codes: 0 independent · 1 violation · 2 usage, unreadable file, or no
    25	#             round block in the transcript
    26	# =============================================================================
    27	set -euo pipefail
    28	export LC_ALL=C
    29	
    30	usage() { sed -n '/^# Usage:/,/^# Exit codes/p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; }
    31	
    32	TRANSCRIPT=""
    33	MIN_AVG="2"
    34	JSON=0
    35	while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    36	  case "$1" in
    37	    --min-average)
    38	      [[ $# -ge 2 ]] || { echo "check-round-independence.sh: --min-average needs a number" >&2; exit 2; }
    39	      MIN_AVG="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    40	    --json) JSON=1; shift ;;
    41	    --help|-h) usage; exit 0 ;;
    42	    --) shift; [[ $# -ge 1 ]] && { TRANSCRIPT="$1"; shift; } ;;
    43	    -*) echo "check-round-independence.sh: unknown flag $1" >&2; exit 2 ;;
    44	    *)
    45	      [[ -z "$TRANSCRIPT" ]] || { echo "check-round-independence.sh: one transcript only" >&2; exit 2; }
    46	      TRANSCRIPT="$1"; shift ;;
    47	  esac
    48	done
    49	
    50	[[ -n "$TRANSCRIPT" ]] || { echo "check-round-independence.sh: transcript path required" >&2; usage >&2; exit 2; }
    51	[[ -f "$TRANSCRIPT" && -r "$TRANSCRIPT" ]] || { echo "check-round-independence.sh: cannot read $TRANSCRIPT" >&2; exit 2; }
    52	[[ "$MIN_AVG" =~ ^[0-9]+([.][0-9]+)?$ ]] || { echo "check-round-independence.sh: --min-average must be a non-negative number, got '$MIN_AVG'" >&2; exit 2; }
    53	command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "check-round-independence.sh: jq is required" >&2; exit 2; }
    54	
    55	BLOCK_RE='<!--[[:space:]]*round:[[:space:]]*[0-9]+[[:space:]]*;[[:space:]]*questions:[[:space:]]*\[.*\][[:space:]]*-->'
    56	
    57	# One JSON object per block: {round, questions} or {round, malformed}. grep exits
    58	# 1 on no match, which is the "no block" case below, not an error.
    59	blocks="$(grep -oE "$BLOCK_RE" "$TRANSCRIPT" || true)"
    60	if [[ -z "$blocks" ]]; then
    61	  echo "check-round-independence.sh: no <!-- round: N; questions: [...] --> block in $TRANSCRIPT" >&2
    62	  exit 2
    63	fi
    64

     1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# loa-decisions-surface.sh: SessionStart hook that surfaces pending decision rows.
     4	#
     5	# Prints up to 10 `proposed` then `open` rows of grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml (id, status,
     6	# summary only) so the operator sees what awaits /decisions confirm. DEFAULT-OFF: gated on
     7	# `decisions.surface_at_session_start` (default false) in .loa.config.yaml.
     8	#
     9	# CONTRACT (observability, never a gate; same as loa-kf-surface.sh):
    10	#   - Exits 0 on every path and never blocks a session.
    11	#   - Disabled, no config, or no Mike Farah yq v4: prints nothing.
    12	#   - Enabled but the ledger is unreadable or has an unknown schema_version: one
    13	#     "[DECISIONS] WARNING ..." line on stdout.
    14	#   - Enabled and healthy: the block on stdout (SessionStart injects stdout as context);
    15	#     nothing when no row is open or proposed and no marker is stale.
    16	#   - A stale .run/unattended.json (another session, or older than
    17	#     decisions.unattended_marker_ttl_hours, default 24) adds one notice line.
    18	#
    19	# TRUST BOUNDARY: row text is agent-authored and UNTRUSTED. Only id, status and summary are
    20	#   read; each summary is control-stripped (C0, C1, U+2028/9), angle brackets are replaced so
    21	#   no tag can close the fence, and it is capped at 100 characters. The whole block is then
    22	#   wrapped by the L6 data fence, sanitize_for_session_start L6 <block> --max-chars 2000
    23	#   (context-isolation-lib.sh). Without that sanitizer the block is not printed.
    24	# =============================================================================
    25	set -uo pipefail
    26	
    27	HOOK_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
    28	REPO_ROOT="$(cd "${HOOK_DIR}/../../.." && pwd)"
    29	
    30	# Test seam (mirrors loa-kf-surface.sh): overrides are honoured only under
    31	# LOA_DEC_SURFACE_TEST_MODE=1 with a bats marker present.
    32	_dec_test_mode_active() {
    33	  [[ "${LOA_DEC_SURFACE_TEST_MODE:-0}" == "1" ]] || return 1
    34	  [[ -n "${BATS_TEST_FILENAME:-}" || -n "${BATS_VERSION:-}" ]]
    35	}
    36	
    37	command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 0
    38	[[ "$(yq --version 2>&1 || true)" == *mikefarah*"version v4."* ]] || exit 0
    39	command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 0
    40	
    41	config_path="${REPO_ROOT}/.loa.config.yaml"
    42	enabled="false"
    43	if _dec_test_mode_active && [[ -n "${LOA_DEC_SURFACE_TEST_CONFIG-}" ]]; then
    44	  enabled="${LOA_DEC_SURFACE_TEST_CONFIG}"
    45	elif [[ -f "$config_path" ]]; then
    46	  enabled="$(yq '.decisions.surface_at_session_start // false' "$config_path" 2>/dev/null || echo false)"
    47	fi
    48	[[ "$enabled" == "true" ]] || exit 0
    49	
    50	LEDGER="${REPO_ROOT}/grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml"
    51	RUN_DIR="${REPO_ROOT}/.run"
    52	if _dec_test_mode_active; then
    53	  [[ -n "${LOA_DECISIONS_FILE:-}" ]] && LEDGER="${LOA_DECISIONS_FILE}"
    54	  [[ -n "${LOA_DEC_SURFACE_RUN_DIR:-}" ]] && RUN_DIR="${LOA_DEC_SURFACE_RUN_DIR}"
    55	fi
    56	
    57	if [[ ! -r "$LEDGER" ]]; then
    58	  echo "[DECISIONS] WARNING: the decision ledger is unreadable at grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml; the surface is enabled but degraded."
    59	  exit 0
    60	fi
    61	doc="$(yq -o=json -I0 '.' "$LEDGER" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    62	if [[ -z "$doc" ]] || ! printf '%s' "$doc" | jq -e '.schema_version == 1 and ((.decisions // []) | type == "array")' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    63	  echo "[DECISIONS] WARNING: grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml does not parse or has an unknown schema_version; the surface is enabled but degraded."
    64	  exit 0
    65	fi
    66	
    67	# Rows: proposed first, then open; fields reduced to a safe id, the status and a cleaned summary.
    68	rows="$(printf '%s' "$doc" | jq -r '
    69	  def clean: tostring | gsub("[[:cntrl:]\u0080-\u009f  ]"; " ") | gsub("<"; "‹") | gsub(">"; "›")
    70	             | gsub("`"; "‘") | gsub("  +"; " ") | sub("^ "; "") | sub(" $"; "");

    72	  [ (.decisions // [])[] | objects | select(.status == "proposed" or .status == "open") ]
    73	  | (map(select(.status == "proposed")) + map(select(.status == "open"))) as $r
    74	  | "C\t\($r | map(select(.status == "proposed")) | length)\t\($r | map(select(.status == "open")) | length)",
    75	    ($r[0:10][] | "R\t\((.id // "") | tostring | gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9-]"; "") | .[0:16])\t\(.status)\t\((.summary // "") | clean | cap)")

    77	
    78	n_prop=0; n_open=0; lines=()
    79	while IFS=$'\t' read -r kind a b c; do
    80	  case "$kind" in
    81	    C) n_prop="$a"; n_open="$b" ;;
    82	    R) lines+=("- ${a} ${b}: ${c}") ;;
    83	  esac
    84	done <<< "$rows"
    85	
    86	# Stale unattended marker (the writer ignores it; the notice tells the operator to clear it).
    87	stale_note=""
    88	marker="${RUN_DIR}/unattended.json"
    89	if [[ -f "$marker" ]]; then
    90	  ttl="$(yq '.decisions.unattended_marker_ttl_hours // 24' "$config_path" 2>/dev/null || echo 24)"
    91	  [[ "$ttl" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$ttl" -gt 0 ]] || ttl=24
    92	  sid="$(jq -r '.session_id // empty' "$marker" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    93	  ca="$(jq -r '.created_at // empty' "$marker" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    94	  ep=""
    95	  if [[ -n "$ca" ]]; then
    96	    # shellcheck source=/dev/null
    97	    ep="$( (source "${REPO_ROOT}/.claude/scripts/compat-lib.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1; _date_to_epoch "$ca") 2>/dev/null || true)"
    98	  fi
    99	  sess="${CLAUDE_SESSION_ID:-${CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID:-}}"
   100	  if [[ ! "$ep" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || (( $(date -u +%s) - ep > ttl * 3600 )) || [[ -n "$sess" && -n "$sid" && "$sid" != "$sess" ]]; then
   101	    stale_note="[DECISIONS] .run/unattended.json is stale (other session or older than ${ttl} h): ignored; clear it with /decisions clear-unattended"
   102	  fi
   103	fi
   104	
   105	total=$(( n_prop + n_open ))
   106	[[ "$total" -gt 0 || -n "$stale_note" ]] || exit 0
   107	
   108	block="$(
   109	  if [[ "$total" -gt 0 ]]; then
   110	    echo "[DECISIONS] ${n_prop} proposed, ${n_open} open (grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml):"
   111	    printf '%s\n' "${lines[@]}"
   112	    if [[ "$total" -gt 10 ]]; then echo "... and $(( total - 10 )) more: dec-write-lib.sh list --status proposed,open"; fi
   113	  fi
   114	  [[ -z "$stale_note" ]] || echo "$stale_note"
   115	  if [[ "$n_prop" -gt 0 ]]; then echo "Confirm proposed rows with /decisions confirm."; fi
   116	)"
   117	
   118	fenced="$( (source "${REPO_ROOT}/.claude/scripts/lib/context-isolation-lib.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
   119	            && sanitize_for_session_start L6 "$block" --max-chars 2000) 2>/dev/null || true)"
   120	if [[ "$fenced" == *"<untrusted-content"* ]]; then
   121	  printf '%s\n' "$fenced"
   122	else
   123	  echo "[DECISIONS] WARNING: ${n_prop} proposed, ${n_open} open; the L6 sanitizer is unavailable, so rows are not shown. Run: .claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh list --status proposed,open"
   124	fi
   125	exit 0

    19	# TRUST BOUNDARY: row text is agent-authored and UNTRUSTED. Only id, status and summary are
    20	#   read; each summary is control-stripped (C0, C1, U+2028/9), angle brackets are replaced so
    21	#   no tag can close the fence, and it is capped at 100 characters. The whole block is then
    22	#   wrapped by the L6 data fence, sanitize_for_session_start L6 <block> --max-chars 2000
    23	#   (context-isolation-lib.sh). Without that sanitizer the block is not printed.
    24	# =============================================================================
    25	set -uo pipefail
    26	
    27	HOOK_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
    28	REPO_ROOT="$(cd "${HOOK_DIR}/../../.." && pwd)"

    30	# Test seam (mirrors loa-kf-surface.sh): overrides are honoured only under
    31	# LOA_DEC_SURFACE_TEST_MODE=1 with a bats marker present.
    32	_dec_test_mode_active() {
    33	  [[ "${LOA_DEC_SURFACE_TEST_MODE:-0}" == "1" ]] || return 1
    34	  [[ -n "${BATS_TEST_FILENAME:-}" || -n "${BATS_VERSION:-}" ]]
    35	}
    36	
    37	command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 0
    38	[[ "$(yq --version 2>&1 || true)" == *mikefarah*"version v4."* ]] || exit 0
    39	command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 0
    40	
    41	config_path="${REPO_ROOT}/.loa.config.yaml"
    42	enabled="false"
    43	if _dec_test_mode_active && [[ -n "${LOA_DEC_SURFACE_TEST_CONFIG-}" ]]; then
    44	  enabled="${LOA_DEC_SURFACE_TEST_CONFIG}"
    45	elif [[ -f "$config_path" ]]; then
    46	  enabled="$(yq '.decisions.surface_at_session_start // false' "$config_path" 2>/dev/null || echo false)"
    47	fi
    48	[[ "$enabled" == "true" ]] || exit 0
    49	
    50	LEDGER="${REPO_ROOT}/grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml"
    51	RUN_DIR="${REPO_ROOT}/.run"
    52	if _dec_test_mode_active; then
    53	  [[ -n "${LOA_DECISIONS_FILE:-}" ]] && LEDGER="${LOA_DECISIONS_FILE}"
    54	  [[ -n "${LOA_DEC_SURFACE_RUN_DIR:-}" ]] && RUN_DIR="${LOA_DEC_SURFACE_RUN_DIR}"
    55	fi
    56	
    57	if [[ ! -r "$LEDGER" ]]; then
    58	  echo "[DECISIONS] WARNING: the decision ledger is unreadable at grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml; the surface is enabled but degraded."
    59	  exit 0
    60	fi
    61	doc="$(yq -o=json -I0 '.' "$LEDGER" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    62	if [[ -z "$doc" ]] || ! printf '%s' "$doc" | jq -e '.schema_version == 1 and ((.decisions // []) | type == "array")' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    63	  echo "[DECISIONS] WARNING: grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml does not parse or has an unknown schema_version; the surface is enabled but degraded."
    64	  exit 0
    65	fi
    66	
    67	# Rows: proposed first, then open; fields reduced to a safe id, the status and a cleaned summary.
    68	rows="$(printf '%s' "$doc" | jq -r '
    69	  def clean: tostring | gsub("[[:cntrl:]\u0080-\u009f  ]"; " ") | gsub("<"; "‹") | gsub(">"; "›")
    70	             | gsub("`"; "‘") | gsub("  +"; " ") | sub("^ "; "") | sub(" $"; "");
    71	  def cap: if length > 100 then .[0:99] + "…" else . end;
    72	  [ (.decisions // [])[] | objects | select(.status == "proposed" or .status == "open") ]
    73	  | (map(select(.status == "proposed")) + map(select(.status == "open"))) as $r
    74	  | "C\t\($r | map(select(.status == "proposed")) | length)\t\($r | map(select(.status == "open")) | length)",
    75	    ($r[0:10][] | "R\t\((.id // "") | tostring | gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9-]"; "") | .[0:16])\t\(.status)\t\((.summary // "") | clean | cap)")
    76	' 2>/dev/null || true)"
    77	
    78	n_prop=0; n_open=0; lines=()
    79	while IFS=$'\t' read -r kind a b c; do
    80	  case "$kind" in
    81	    C) n_prop="$a"; n_open="$b" ;;
    82	    R) lines+=("- ${a} ${b}: ${c}") ;;
    83	  esac
    84	done <<< "$rows"
    85	
    86	# Stale unattended marker (the writer ignores it; the notice tells the operator to clear it).
    87	stale_note=""
    88	marker="${RUN_DIR}/unattended.json"
    89	if [[ -f "$marker" ]]; then
    90	  ttl="$(yq '.decisions.unattended_marker_ttl_hours // 24' "$config_path" 2>/dev/null || echo 24)"
    91	  [[ "$ttl" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$ttl" -gt 0 ]] || ttl=24
    92	  sid="$(jq -r '.session_id // empty' "$marker" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    93	  ca="$(jq -r '.created_at // empty' "$marker" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    94	  ep=""
    95	  if [[ -n "$ca" ]]; then
    96	    # shellcheck source=/dev/null
    97	    ep="$( (source "${REPO_ROOT}/.claude/scripts/compat-lib.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1; _date_to_epoch "$ca") 2>/dev/null || true)"
    98	  fi
    99	  sess="${CLAUDE_SESSION_ID:-${CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID:-}}"
   100	  if [[ ! "$ep" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || (( $(date -u +%s) - ep > ttl * 3600 )) || [[ -n "$sess" && -n "$sid" && "$sid" != "$sess" ]]; then
   101	    stale_note="[DECISIONS] .run/unattended.json is stale (other session or older than ${ttl} h): ignored; clear it with /decisions clear-unattended"
   102	  fi
   103	fi
   104	
   105	total=$(( n_prop + n_open ))
   106	[[ "$total" -gt 0 || -n "$stale_note" ]] || exit 0
   107	
   108	block="$(
   109	  if [[ "$total" -gt 0 ]]; then
   110	    echo "[DECISIONS] ${n_prop} proposed, ${n_open} open (grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml):"
   111	    printf '%s\n' "${lines[@]}"
   112	    if [[ "$total" -gt 10 ]]; then echo "... and $(( total - 10 )) more: dec-write-lib.sh list --status proposed,open"; fi
   113	  fi
   114	  [[ -z "$stale_note" ]] || echo "$stale_note"
   115	  if [[ "$n_prop" -gt 0 ]]; then echo "Confirm proposed rows with /decisions confirm."; fi
   116	)"
   117	
   118	fenced="$( (source "${REPO_ROOT}/.claude/scripts/lib/context-isolation-lib.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
   119	            && sanitize_for_session_start L6 "$block" --max-chars 2000) 2>/dev/null || true)"
   120	if [[ "$fenced" == *"<untrusted-content"* ]]; then
   121	  printf '%s\n' "$fenced"
   122	else
   123	  echo "[DECISIONS] WARNING: ${n_prop} proposed, ${n_open} open; the L6 sanitizer is unavailable, so rows are not shown. Run: .claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh list --status proposed,open"
   124	fi
   125	exit 0

563	  local rat fu; rat="$(san1 "$(o rationale)")"; fu="$(san1 "$(o follow-up)")"
564	  [[ -n "$rat" ]] || die "reject: --rationale is required"
565	  [[ -n "$fu" ]] || die "reject: --follow-up is required (a bead id or NOTES anchor, so the correction propagates)"

567	  acquire_lock "$TARGET"
568	  local old r st rb by; old="$(read_ledger "$TARGET")"; r="$(row_by_id "$old" "$id")"
569	  [[ -n "$r" ]] || die "reject: unknown id ${id}"
570	  st="$(printf '%s' "$r" | jq -r '.status')"; rb="$(recorded_by)"
571	  case "$st" in
572	    open|proposed) if is_operator_call && ! is_unattended; then by="operator:${OPERATOR_CMD}"; else by="agent:${rb}"; fi ;;

595	  acquire_lock "$TARGET"

599	  [[ "$st" == "decided" ]] || die "supersede: ${oid} is ${st}; only a decided row is superseded (reject an open or proposed row instead)"

611	  fi
612	  replace_row "$r"
613	  verify_and_swap "$old" 1 "$(jq -cn --arg a "$oid" --arg b "$nid" '[$a, $b]')"

618	op_import(){
619	  preflight
620	  local from; from="$(o from)"; [[ -n "$from" ]] || usage "import --from <pending file> required"

622	  if has file; then resolve_target write; else
623	    [[ $IS_WORKTREE -eq 0 ]] || die "import runs in the main checkout (this is a linked worktree)"
624	    local why; if why="$(ci_blocked)"; then die "refused: ${why} is set"; fi
625	    TARGET="$LIVE"; TARGET_KIND="live"; [[ -f "$TARGET" ]] || die "ledger not found: $TARGET"

632	  # Allocate ids in file order, then rewrite every PEND reference inside the imported rows.
633	  local map="{}" pid i next cur="$old"
634	  for (( i = 0; i < n; i++ )); do
635	    pid="$(printf '%s' "$pend" | jq -r --argjson i "$i" '.decisions[$i].id')"

640	  done

642	  local rows touched r; rows="$(printf '%s' "$pend" | jq -c --argjson m "$map" '

644	      .decisions[] | walk(if type == "string" then rw else . end)')"
645	  touched="$(jq -cn --argjson m "$map" '[$m[]]')"

660	op_list(){
661	  command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "list: jq is required"
662	  command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "list: Mike Farah yq v4 is required"

670	    printf '%s' "$j" | jq -e '(.decisions // []) | type == "array"' >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "list: no decisions sequence in ${TARGET}"
671	  fi

674	  printf '%s' "$j" | jq -r --arg fmt "$fmt" --arg st "$(o status)" --arg vo "$voice" --arg nv "$(o not-decided-by)" \
675	    --arg cy "$(o cycle)" --arg since "$(o since)" --arg sp "$(o source-prefix)" --arg se "$(o source-epic)" --arg ids "$ids" '
676	    def csv: if . == "" then [] else split(",") | map(select(length > 0)) end;
677	    def cl: tostring | gsub("[[:cntrl:]]"; " ");
678	    def mc: cl | gsub("\\|"; "\\|");
679	    ($st | csv) as $S | ($vo | csv) as $V | ($nv | csv) as $NV | ($ids | csv) as $I
680	    | [ (.decisions // [])[]
681	        | (.decided_by // .proposed_by // "") as $voice | (.status // "") as $status | (.id // "") as $id
682	        | select(($S | length) == 0 or ($S | index($status)))
683	        | select(($V | length) == 0 or ($V | index($voice)))
684	        | select(($NV | length) == 0 or (($NV | index($voice)) | not))
685	        | select($cy == "" or .cycle == $cy)
686	        | select($since == "" or ((.created_at // "") >= $since))
687	        | select($sp == "" or ((.source // "") | startswith($sp)))
688	        | select($se == "" or ((.source // "") | startswith("map:" + $se + "/")))
689	        | select(($I | length) == 0 or ($I | index($id)))
690	        | . + {voice: $voice} ] as $rows
691	    | if $fmt == "json" then ($rows | tojson)
692	      elif $fmt == "tsv" then ($rows[] | [.id, .status, .voice, (.summary // ""), (.source // "")] | map(cl) | join("\t"))
693	      else
694	        if ($rows | length) == 0 then "_None: every decision in this run was the operator'"'"'s._"
695	        else ("| Decision | Voice | Status | Why | Source |", "|---|---|---|---|---|",
696	              ($rows[] | "| \((.summary // "") | mc) (\(.id)) | \(.voice | mc) | \(.status | mc) | \((.rationale // "") | mc) | \((.source // "") | mc) |"),
697	              "Confirm with /decisions confirm.")
698	        end
699	      end'
700	}

702	op_context(){
703	  PRD_PATH="$(o prd)"
704	  if has set-unattended; then
705	    local reason; reason="$(san1 "$(o reason)")"; [[ -n "$reason" ]] || usage "context --set-unattended needs --reason"

707	    mkdir -p "${PROJECT_ROOT}/.run"
708	    local m="${PROJECT_ROOT}/.run/unattended.json" t
709	    t="$(mktemp "${m}.XXXXXX")"
710	    jq -n --arg r "$reason" --arg s "$(session_id)" --arg c "$(now_utc)" '{reason: $r, session_id: $s, created_at: $c}' > "$t"
711	    mv -f "$t" "$m"
712	    log "dec-write: unattended marker written (${m#"${PROJECT_ROOT}/"}); it expires after $(ttl_hours) h or when the session changes"
713	    echo unattended; return 0
714	  fi
715	  if has clear; then
716	    is_operator_call || die "context --clear runs only from the operator-only /decisions command (--recorded-by ${OPERATOR_CMD})"
717	    local mk="${PROJECT_ROOT}/.run/unattended.json"
718	    rm -f -- "$mk"
719	    log "dec-write: unattended marker cleared"
720	  fi
721	  local sig; sig="$(ctx_signals)"
722	  if [[ -n "$sig" ]]; then echo unattended; else echo interactive; fi
723	  if has why; then
724	    if [[ -n "$sig" ]]; then printf '%s\n' "$sig" | sed 's/^/signal: /'; else echo "signal: none"; fi
725	    local d ms; while IFS= read -r d; do ms="$(marker_state "$d/unattended.json")"; if [[ "$ms" == "stale" ]]; then echo "note: stale marker ignored: $d/unattended.json"; fi; done < <(run_dirs)
726	  fi
727	  return 0
728	}

730	case "$CMD" in
731	  new) op_new ;;
732	  decide) op_decide ;;
733	  confirm) op_confirm ;;
734	  reject) op_reject ;;
735	  supersede) op_supersede ;;

740	  *) usage "unknown command: $CMD (new|decide|confirm|reject|supersede|import|list|context)" ;;
741	esac

   337	# translation (C-D5, cycle-120)
   338	# =============================================================================
   339	# Resolution bases, in order — hygiene-report.md lives under reality/, other
   340	# /ride artifacts live directly under grimoires/loa/, and a citation may
   341	# already be qualified with either prefix (in which case the repo-root base
   342	# resolves it directly).
   343	_translation_find_report() {
   344	    local name="$1" base
   345	    for base in "$PROJECT_ROOT" "$PROJECT_ROOT/grimoires/loa" "$PROJECT_ROOT/grimoires/loa/reality"; do
   346	        if [[ -f "$base/$name" ]]; then
   347	            echo "$base/$name"
   348	            return 0
   349	        fi
   350	    done
   351	    return 1
   352	}
   353	
   354	# Citation-resolution scan for one file. Matches both `(path:L##[-L##])`
   355	# and bare table-cell `path:L##` with a single regex — the surrounding
   356	# parens/pipes are not part of the match, so one pass covers both forms.
   357	_validate_translation_citations() {
   358	    local f="$1" in_fence=false lineno=0 line
   359	    # Held in a single-quoted variable (never a bare literal in a =~/== RHS)
   360	    # so the parser never treats the backticks as command substitution.
   361	    local fence='```'
   362	    while IFS= read -r line || [[ -n "$line" ]]; do
   363	        lineno=$((lineno + 1))
   364	
   365	        if [[ "$line" == "$fence"* || "$line" =~ ^[[:space:]]+${fence} ]]; then
   366	            [[ "$in_fence" == true ]] && in_fence=false || in_fence=true
   367	            continue
   368	        fi
   369	        [[ "$in_fence" == true ]] && continue
   370	
   371	        # markdown-link / bare-URL forms — skip wholesale to avoid false
   372	        # positives (a URL's "domain.tld/path:L##"-shaped substring is not
   373	        # a citation into this repo).
   374	        [[ "$line" == *'](http'* || "$line" == *'://'* ]] && continue
   375	
   376	        # R2 review (cycle-120): the incremental `while [[ =~ ]]` scan below is
   377	        # superlinear on a single very long path-dense line (LLM translation
   378	        # docs routinely carry wide tables / pasted logs on one unwrapped line),
   379	        # which would hang this MUST gate with no output. Cap line length; a
   380	        # citation the gate must resolve never needs 2000+ chars on one line.
   381	        # WARN rather than silently skip so an over-long line is visible.
   382	        if (( ${#line} > 2000 )); then
   383	            warnings+=("line ${lineno} exceeds 2000 chars — citation scan skipped for this line (wrap long tables/logs)")
   384	            continue
   385	        fi
   386	
   387	        local rest="$line"
   388	        while [[ "$rest" =~ ([A-Za-z0-9_./-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9]{1,6}):L([0-9]+)(-L[0-9]+)? ]]; do
   389	            local cited_path="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
   390	            local cited_startline="${BASH_REMATCH[2]}"
   391	            local match_full="${BASH_REMATCH[0]}"
   392	            rest="${rest#*"$match_full"}"
   393	
   394	            # {...}-placeholder citations (e.g. `{file}:L{N}`) never reach
   395	            # here — the regex requires a real dotted extension and real
   396	            # digits — but guard explicitly in case a brace rides along a
   397	            # real-looking path.
   398	            [[ "$cited_path" == *'{'* || "$cited_path" == *'}'* ]] && continue
   399	
   400	            local resolved="" base
   401	            for base in "$PROJECT_ROOT" "$PROJECT_ROOT/grimoires/loa" "$PROJECT_ROOT/grimoires/loa/reality"; do
   402	                if [[ -f "$base/$cited_path" ]]; then
   403	                    resolved="$base/$cited_path"
   404	                    break
   405	                fi
   406	            done
   407	
   408	            if [[ -z "$resolved" ]]; then
   409	                violations+=("CITATION UNRESOLVED: '$cited_path:L$cited_startline' cited at $f:$lineno does not resolve under repo-root, grimoires/loa/, or grimoires/loa/reality/ — fix the path or remove the citation")
   410	                continue
   411	            fi
   412	
   413	            local total_lines
   414	            total_lines=$(wc -l < "$resolved" | tr -d ' ')
   415	            if [[ "$total_lines" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && (( cited_startline > total_lines )); then
   416	                violations+=("CITATION LINE OUT OF RANGE: '$cited_path:L$cited_startline' cited at $f:$lineno but $resolved has only $total_lines lines — fix the cited line number")
   417	            fi
   418	        done
   419	    done < "$f"
   420	}

   230	validate_sprint() {
   231	    local sprint_headings
   232	    sprint_headings=$(grep -nE '^## Sprint [0-9]' -- "$FILE" || true)
   233	
   234	    if [[ -z "$sprint_headings" ]]; then
   235	        violations+=("no '## Sprint N' blocks found — sprint.md must contain at least one sprint block")
   236	        return
   237	    fi
   238	
   239	    local last_sprint_heading="" last_sprint_lineno=0
   240	    while IFS=: read -r lineno heading; do
   241	        [[ -z "$lineno" ]] && continue
   242	        last_sprint_heading="$heading"
   243	        last_sprint_lineno="$lineno"
   244	        local block
   245	        block=$(awk -v start="$lineno" '
   246	            NR > start && /^## Sprint [0-9]/ { exit }
   247	            NR > start { print }
   248	        ' < "$FILE")
   249	        local sec
   250	        for sec in "${SPRINT_REQUIRED_SECTIONS[@]}"; do

   253	            fi
   254	        done
   255	        for sec in "${SPRINT_WARN_SECTIONS[@]}"; do

   267	        found && /^## / { found=0 }

   271	    local body_goal_ids

   276	            if ! grep -qwF "$gid" <<< "$appendix_body"; then

   336	# =============================================================================
   337	# translation (C-D5, cycle-120)
   338	# =============================================================================
   339	# Resolution bases, in order — hygiene-report.md lives under reality/, other
   340	# /ride artifacts live directly under grimoires/loa/, and a citation may
   341	# already be qualified with either prefix (in which case the repo-root base
   342	# resolves it directly).
   343	_translation_find_report() {
   344	    local name="$1" base
   345	    for base in "$PROJECT_ROOT" "$PROJECT_ROOT/grimoires/loa" "$PROJECT_ROOT/grimoires/loa/reality"; do
   346	        if [[ -f "$base/$name" ]]; then
   347	            echo "$base/$name"
   348	            return 0
   349	        fi
   350	    done
   351	    return 1

   353	
   354	# Citation-resolution scan for one file. Matches both `(path:L##[-L##])`
   355	# and bare table-cell `path:L##` with a single regex — the surrounding
   356	# parens/pipes are not part of the match, so one pass covers both forms.
   357	_validate_translation_citations() {
   358	    local f="$1" in_fence=false lineno=0 line
   359	    # Held in a single-quoted variable (never a bare literal in a =~/== RHS)
   360	    # so the parser never treats the backticks as command substitution.
   361	    local fence='```'
   362	    while IFS= read -r line || [[ -n "$line" ]]; do
   363	        lineno=$((lineno + 1))
   364	
   365	        if [[ "$line" == "$fence"* || "$line" =~ ^[[:space:]]+${fence} ]]; then
   366	            [[ "$in_fence" == true ]] && in_fence=false || in_fence=true
   367	            continue
   368	        fi
   369	        [[ "$in_fence" == true ]] && continue
   370	
   371	        # markdown-link / bare-URL forms — skip wholesale to avoid false
   372	        # positives (a URL's "domain.tld/path:L##"-shaped substring is not
   373	        # a citation into this repo).
   374	        [[ "$line" == *'](http'* || "$line" == *'://'* ]] && continue
   375	
   376	        # R2 review (cycle-120): the incremental `while [[ =~ ]]` scan below is
   377	        # superlinear on a single very long path-dense line (LLM translation
   378	        # docs routinely carry wide tables / pasted logs on one unwrapped line),
   379	        # which would hang this MUST gate with no output. Cap line length; a
   380	        # citation the gate must resolve never needs 2000+ chars on one line.
   381	        # WARN rather than silently skip so an over-long line is visible.
   382	        if (( ${#line} > 2000 )); then
   383	            warnings+=("line ${lineno} exceeds 2000 chars — citation scan skipped for this line (wrap long tables/logs)")
   384	            continue
   385	        fi
   386	
   387	        local rest="$line"
   388	        while [[ "$rest" =~ ([A-Za-z0-9_./-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9]{1,6}):L([0-9]+)(-L[0-9]+)? ]]; do
   389	            local cited_path="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
   390	            local cited_startline="${BASH_REMATCH[2]}"
   391	            local match_full="${BASH_REMATCH[0]}"
   392	            rest="${rest#*"$match_full"}"
   393	
   394	            # {...}-placeholder citations (e.g. `{file}:L{N}`) never reach
   395	            # here — the regex requires a real dotted extension and real
   396	            # digits — but guard explicitly in case a brace rides along a
   397	            # real-looking path.
   398	            [[ "$cited_path" == *'{'* || "$cited_path" == *'}'* ]] && continue
   399	
   400	            local resolved="" base
   401	            for base in "$PROJECT_ROOT" "$PROJECT_ROOT/grimoires/loa" "$PROJECT_ROOT/grimoires/loa/reality"; do
   402	                if [[ -f "$base/$cited_path" ]]; then
   403	                    resolved="$base/$cited_path"
   404	                    break
   405	                fi
   406	            done
   407	
   408	            if [[ -z "$resolved" ]]; then
   409	                violations+=("CITATION UNRESOLVED: '$cited_path:L$cited_startline' cited at $f:$lineno does not resolve under repo-root, grimoires/loa/, or grimoires/loa/reality/ — fix the path or remove the citation")
   410	                continue
   411	            fi
   412	
   413	            local total_lines
   414	            total_lines=$(wc -l < "$resolved" | tr -d ' ')
   415	            if [[ "$total_lines" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && (( cited_startline > total_lines )); then
   416	                violations+=("CITATION LINE OUT OF RANGE: '$cited_path:L$cited_startline' cited at $f:$lineno but $resolved has only $total_lines lines — fix the cited line number")
   417	            fi
   418	        done
   419	    done < "$f"
   420	}

   438	_validate_translation_health_score() {
   439	    local files=("$@")
   440	    (( ${#files[@]} == 0 )) && return 0
   441	
   442	    local combined
   443	    combined=$(cat "${files[@]}" 2>/dev/null || true)
   444

   446	    stated=$(printf '%s\n' "$combined" | grep -oiE 'health score[^0-9]{0,10}[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?' | head -1 | grep -oE '[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?$' || true)
   447	    [[ -z "$stated" ]] && return 0

   454

   456	    drift=$(grep -oiE 'drift score:?[[:space:]]*[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?%' -- "$drift_file" | head -1 | grep -oE '[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?' || true)

content.content:
parse_args "$@"
require_jq
if [[ "$MODE" == "tsv" ]]; then collect; exit 0; fi
mkdir -p "${PROJECT_ROOT}/.run"
JSON="$(to_json)"

case "$MODE" in
  json) echo "$JSON" ;;
  validate)
    rc=0
    bad="$(echo "$JSON" | jq -r '[.families[][] | select((.id|length)==0 or (.path|length)==0)] | length')"
    [[ "$bad" != "0" ]] && { echo "::error::[GRIMOIRE-INDEX] $bad entries missing id/path" >&2; rc=1; }
    # KF Index drift — FAIL-ON-DRIFT assertion (cycle-115 D1). The derived kf
    # Index is now AUTHORITATIVE: one row is generated per ## KF-NNN: heading
    # (source of truth). raw_heads is the literal heading count; gen_kf is the
    # number of rows emitted (deduplicated by id). On a clean file these are
    # equal. A mismatch means a heading id is DUPLICATED (two entries claiming
    # one KF-NNN — a defect in the append-only log) or the generator silently
    # dropped/added an entry — either way the derived Index no longer faithfully
    # mirrors the headings. That is a hard error, not an informational warning.
    raw_heads=$(grep -cE '^## KF-[0-9]+:' "${G}/known-failures.md" 2>/dev/null || true); raw_heads=${raw_heads:-0}
    gen_kf=$(echo "$JSON" | jq -r '.counts.kf // 0')
    if [[ "$raw_heads" != "$gen_kf" ]]; then
      echo "::error::[GRIMOIRE-INDEX] generated kf Index has ${gen_kf} rows but known-failures.md has ${raw_heads} ## KF- headings — derived Index drifted from source of truth (duplicate heading id, or a dropped/added entry)." >&2
      rc=1
    fi
    # The hand-maintained "## Index" table inside known-failures.md is being
    # superseded by this derived Index; its staleness is informational only
    # (human-edit scope, tracked separately) and does NOT fail validation.
    hand_rows=$(awk '/^## Index/{i=1;next} i&&/^## /{exit} i' "${G}/known-failures.md" 2>/dev/null | grep -cE '^\| *\[KF-[0-9]+\]' || true); hand_rows=${hand_rows:-0}
    if [[ "$hand_rows" != "$raw_heads" ]]; then
      echo "::warning::[GRIMOIRE-INDEX] known-failures.md hand ## Index table lists ${hand_rows} KF rows but there are ${raw_heads} ## KF- entries — hand table is stale (informational; the derived Index is authoritative)." >&2
    fi
    [[ $rc -eq 0 ]] && log "grimoire-index: valid ($(echo "$JSON" | jq -r '.total') entries; kf=${gen_kf}, headings=${raw_heads}, hand-table=${hand_rows})"
    exit $rc ;;
  write)
    bad="$(echo "$JSON" | jq -r '[.families[][] | select((.id|length)==0 or (.path|length)==0 or (.family|test("[^a-z]")))] | length')"
    if [[ "$bad" != "0" ]]; then echo "::error::[GRIMOIRE-INDEX] refusing to write — $bad malformed records (id/path/family). Likely a corrupt source filename." >&2; exit 1; fi
    exec 9>"$LOCK"; flock 9 2>/dev/null || true
    tmpj="$(mktemp)"; printf '%s\n' "$JSON" > "$tmpj"; mv "$tmpj" "$OUT_JSON"
    tmpm="$(mktemp)"; render_md "$JSON" > "$tmpm"; mv "$tmpm" "$OUT_MD"
    log "grimoire-index: wrote ${OUT_MD#$PROJECT_ROOT/} + ${OUT_JSON#$PROJECT_ROOT/} ($(echo "$JSON" | jq -r '.total') entries)" ;;
esac

     1	#!/usr/bin/env bats
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# user-invoked-commands.bats: the operator-only command allowlist (FR-8, D-8.3)
     4	# =============================================================================
     5	# `.claude/data/user-invoked-commands.txt` lists commands carrying
     6	# `disable-model-invocation: true`. The harness refuses those to the Skill
     7	# tool (tests/unit/user-invoked-harness.bats), so no other command or skill
     8	# body may tell the model to run one as a step. Asserts:
     9	#   1. every listed command file exists and carries the flag
    10	#   2. no other body has an operative line for a listed name
    11	#   3. every command file carrying the flag is listed
    12	#   4. no SKILL.md allowed-tools grants dec-write-lib.sh confirm, supersede
    13	#      or context --clear (those are reachable only through /decisions)
    14	# Each check is a function over a root directory, proved against fixtures.
    15	
    16	setup() {
    17	    PROJECT_ROOT="$(cd "$BATS_TEST_DIRNAME/../.." && pwd)"
    18	    export LC_ALL=C
    19	}
    20	
    21	# list_names <root>: the allowlisted names, comments and blanks stripped
    22	list_names() {
    23	    sed -e 's/#.*$//' -e 's/[[:space:]]*$//' -e 's/^[[:space:]]*//' \
    24	        "$1/.claude/data/user-invoked-commands.txt" | grep -v '^$' || true
    25	}
    26	
    27	# frontmatter <file>: the first YAML frontmatter block (empty when none)
    28	frontmatter() {
    29	    awk 'NR==1 && $0!="---"{exit} /^---[[:space:]]*$/{n++; if(n==2) exit; next} n==1{print}' "$1"
    30	}
    31	
    32	has_flag() {
    33	    frontmatter "$1" | grep -Eq '^disable-model-invocation:[[:space:]]*"?true"?[[:space:]]*$'
    34	}
    35	
    36	# check_listed_flagged <root>: prints each listed name whose file is missing or unflagged
    37	check_listed_flagged() {
    38	    local root="$1" name f
    39	    while IFS= read -r name; do
    40	        f="$root/.claude/commands/$name.md"
    41	        if [[ ! -f "$f" ]]; then
    42	            echo "missing: $name"
    43	        elif ! has_flag "$f"; then
    44	            echo "unflagged: $name"
    45	        fi
    46	    done < <(list_names "$root")
    47	}
    48	
    49	# check_flagged_listed <root>: prints each flagged command file not in the list
    50	check_flagged_listed() {
    51	    local root="$1" f name names
    52	    names="$(list_names "$root")"
    53	    for f in "$root"/.claude/commands/*.md; do
    54	        [[ -f "$f" ]] || continue
    55	        has_flag "$f" || continue
    56	        name="$(basename "$f" .md)"
    57	        grep -qxF "$name" <<<"$names" || echo "unlisted: $name"
    58	    done
    59	}
    60	
    61	# check_operative <root>: prints file:line for each operative reference to a
    62	# listed name in a body other than that command's own file
    63	check_operative() {
    64	    local root="$1" name re exempt
    65	    exempt='(^|[^[:alpha:]])(user|operator|human|manually|suggest|recommend|tell|ask)'
    66	    while IFS= read -r name; do
    67	        # SDD D-8.3 pattern, widened: verbs match in any case and may take
    68	        # "the" ("execute /x", "Invoke the /x skill").
    69	        re="([Ee][Xx][Ee][Cc][Uu][Tt][Ee]|[Ii][Nn][Vv][Oo][Kk][Ee]|[Rr][Uu][Nn]|[Cc][Aa][Ll][Ll])[[:space:]]+(the[[:space:]]+)?\`?/${name}([^[:alnum:]_-]|\$)|Skill\\(.*${name}"
    70	        { find "$root/.claude/commands" -name '*.md' -type f 2>/dev/null
    71	          find "$root/.claude/skills" -name '*.md' -type f 2>/dev/null; } |
    72	        while IFS= read -r f; do
    73	            [[ "$f" == "$root/.claude/commands/$name.md" ]] && continue
    74	            grep -nE "$re" "$f" 2>/dev/null | grep -viE "$exempt" |
    75	                sed "s|^|${f#"$root"/}:|" || true
    76	        done
    77	    done < <(list_names "$root")
    78	}
    79

    82	check_operator_ops() {
    83	    local root="$1" f
    84	    while IFS= read -r f; do

    88	    return 0
    89	}

    96	    printf -- '---\nname: beta\ndisable-model-invocation: true\n---\nRun `/alpha` from another command body.\n' > "$r/.claude/commands/beta.md"

#!/usr/bin/env bats
# =============================================================================
# tests/unit/check-round-independence.bats
#
# tools/check-round-independence.sh reads the `<!-- round: N; questions: [...] -->`
# blocks that `interview.pacing: rounds` puts at the end of every round
# (discovering-requirements/resources/REFERENCE.md §Question Pacing) and fails
# when a question depends on another question of the same round, on one never
# asked earlier, when ids repeat without "reasked", or when rounds average
# fewer than --min-average new questions (final round exempt).
# =============================================================================

setup() {
    SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$BATS_TEST_FILENAME")" && pwd)"
    PROJECT_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
    CHECK="$PROJECT_ROOT/tools/check-round-independence.sh"
    FIX="$PROJECT_ROOT/tests/fixtures/rounds"
    T="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/transcript.md"
}

# Write a transcript whose rounds are the given JSON arrays, in order.
transcript() {
    local n=0 arr
    : > "$T"
    for arr in "$@"; do
        n=$((n + 1))
        printf 'Round %d\n\nquestions...\n<!-- round: %d; questions: %s -->\n\n' "$n" "$n" "$arr" >> "$T"
    done
}

@test "RI-1 the independent fixture passes at the default minimum and reports per-round counts" {
    run "$CHECK" "$FIX/independent.md"
    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    [[ "$output" == *"round 1: 3 new question(s) [Q1 Q2 Q3]"* ]]
    [[ "$output" == *"round 3: 1 new question(s), 1 re-asked [Q6 Q7]"* ]]
    [[ "$output" == *"rounds: 4; questions: 8; average: 2.33 per round (final round exempt); min-average: 2"* ]]
    [[ "$output" == *"PASS"* ]]
}

@test "RI-2 the fixture has at least three rounds and --json carries the report fields" {
  [[ "$output" == *"ledger untouched"* ]]
  cmp "$F" "$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/before.yaml"
  # no temp file is left beside the target
  [ -z "$(find "$T" -maxdepth 1 -name 'fixture.yaml.*')" ]
}

@test "dec-write: an unknown schema_version is refused before any write" {

> 
> ## Interview Modes
> 
> The skill resolves `interview_mode` (`interview.mode`, overridden per skill by `interview.per_skill.<skill>`), `pacing` and the input styles in its Config Reading block. These tables say what each value does.
> 
> ### Mode Behavior Table
> 
> | Mode | Questions/Phase | Default pacing | Phase Gates | Gap Skipping |
> |---|---|---|---|---|
> | `thorough` | 3-6 (scales down with context) | `rounds` | All ON | Always ask `min_confirm` |
> | `minimal` | 1-2 | `batch` | `before_generation` only | Skip covered phases |
> 
> An explicit `interview.pacing` wins over the mode default, so a config that sets `sequential` keeps it.
> 
> ### Input Style Resolution
> 
> | Interaction Type | `structured` | `plain` |
> |---|---|---|
> | Routing gates | AskUserQuestion with options | "Continue, go back, or skip ahead?" |
> | Discovery questions | AskUserQuestion with suggested answers | Markdown question, user responds freely |
> | Confirmations | AskUserQuestion (Yes/Correct/Adjust) | "Is this accurate? [yes/corrections]" |
> 
> In `rounds` pacing, a round is one message even when `discovery_questions` is `structured`: present the numbered round as markdown and take the reply as text, because a round can hold more questions than one AskUserQuestion call allows.
> 
> ## Question Pacing
> 
> One key, `interview.pacing`, sets the pacing for the discovery interview, `/architect` Phase 2, `/sprint-plan` Phase 2 and `/chart`. Those skills point here.
> 
> | Pacing | Behavior |
> |---|---|
> | `sequential` | Ask ONE question per turn. Wait for response. Then ask the next. The supported opt-out from rounds. |
> | `batch` | Present 3-6 numbered questions. User responds to all at once. The `minimal` default. |
> | `rounds` | Ask the whole frontier per turn, as below. The `thorough` default. |
> 
> ### Rounds
> 
> 1. **Frontier.** The frontier is every open question whose prerequisites are settled. A question that depends on another question still open waits for a later round. There is no cap on round size.
> 2. **Facts stay out.** A fact (what code, reality files or docs say) is looked up, never asked; only decisions enter a round (Backpressure Protocol, "Fact or decision").
> 3. **Phase scope.** A round runs within the current discovery phase. A question that belongs to a later phase is parked for that phase. Phase gates are unchanged.
> 4. **Format.** Number questions across the session (`Q1`, `Q2`, ...), so ids never restart. Each question has a short title line starting `❓ Q<n>:`, the question worded so that "yes" accepts the recommendation, and a `➡ Recommended:` line giving the answer and its reason, with a citation when there is one. Close the round with the answer prompt and the comment block.
> 5. **Answers.** A bare "yes" accepts every recommendation in the round. A numbered answer (`2: no, keep it local`) overrides that question. If the operator answers some numbers and not others, restate the unanswered ones with their recommendations and ask for confirmation; they take the recommendation only after the operator confirms. A question still unconfirmed is re-asked in the next round.
> 6. **Recompute.** Before the next round, recompute the frontier from the answers: settled questions leave, questions whose prerequisites just settled join. "wrap up" ends the phase.
> 7. **Comment block.** End every round with one HTML comment holding a JSON array, one object per question: `{"id": "Q4", "depends_on": ["Q1"]}`. `depends_on` lists the earlier questions this one needed settled, `[]` when none. A re-asked question keeps its id and carries `"reasked": true`. The block is how `tools/check-round-independence.sh` checks that no question in a round depends on another question in the same round.
> 
> ```
> Round 2 (Functional Requirements)
> 
> ❓ Q4: Ledger location
> Should the decision ledger live at grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml, tracked?
> ➡ Recommended: yes (the spec and two readers already point there; decision-lineage.md:23)
> 
> ❓ Q5: Unattended record
> Should unattended runs write a DEC row for every decision they take for you?
> ➡ Recommended: yes (makes "which did a human decide?" answerable)
> 
> ❓ Q2: Default pacing (re-asked)
> Should rounds be the default pacing for thorough mode?
> ➡ Recommended: yes (one turn per frontier instead of one per question)
> 
> "yes" accepts all three; answer by number to override one.
> <!-- round: 2; questions: [{"id":"Q4","depends_on":[]},{"id":"Q5","depends_on":["Q1"]},{"id":"Q2","depends_on":[],"reasked":true}] -->
> ```
> 
> The checker: `tools/check-round-independence.sh <transcript> [--min-average N] [--json]` exits 0 when every round is independent and the rounds average at least N questions (default 2; the final round is exempt when there are two or more rounds), 1 on a violation, 2 when the transcript has no round block.

content.text:
The pull request should not merge. My verdict is **CHANGES_REQUIRED**, with 10 findings written to `/workspace/review.md`. I reproduced most of them by running the scripts on a scratch copy of `head/`; nothing under `pr/` was changed.

**Most serious:**
1. **Agents can confirm their own decisions** (`dec-write-lib.sh:359`). The "operator-only" check is just the flag `--recorded-by decisions-command`. Any agent with shell access can pass it and get a row recorded as `decided_by: operator`. Marking the command as not model-invocable doesn't help, because the agent never goes through the command — it calls the script directly.
2. **Unattended discovery runs always produce a failing PRD** (`discovering-requirements/SKILL.md:5`). The skill is now told to record each decision with `dec-write-lib.sh new`, but its allowed tools don't let it run that script.
